newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far right scores gains in local election.
newsitem.headline: Austria far right scores gains in local election.

text.p: Austria's ruling Social Democrats lost ground to the far right in local council elections on Sunday in the province of Carinthia, provisional results reported by Austrian state television indicated.
The Social Democrats remained the strongest party in the southern Austrian state and clinched 40.5 percent of the vote, five percent less than in the last local elections six years ago.
The far-right Freedom Party took second place, increasing its share of the vote by almost five percent to 26.07 percent.

The conservative People's Party, which on the federal level is the junior coalition partner of the Social Democrats, slipped to third place with 22.33 percent of the vote, a decline of more than two percent.
Almost 80 percent of 424,254 eligible voters cast ballots in towns and villages where local issues led the election campaign.

The municipal poll was the first test of popularity for the federal government of Chancelllor Viktor Klima, who took over after the surprise resignation of fellow Social Democrat Franz Vranitzky in January.

In the latest nationwide opinion poll, conducted last month, the Social Democrats scored 41 percent, their highest approval rating for two and a half years. The People's Party and the Freedom Party both came in at 23 percent.
